standardApplied.FEE_AND_WAIVER: Settled by DET-FEE-AND-WAIVER-001 (data/rcap-grade-a/fable-packet-factory/DETERMINATION_FEE_AND_WAIVER_STANDARD.json) and applied here in place of this lane's earlier reading. FEE_AND_WAIVER.finding: Re-examined against DET-FEE-AND-WAIVER-001 and reversed. This family carries, word for word, the sentence the determination names as its proven case: "Any filing fee or fee-waiver answer. No held source states a fee, that filing is free, or a waiver procedure - ask the Criminal Division clerk's office (202-879-1373) before filing." That is the third met clause exactly - the packet states that no held source establishes the fee AND names a specific checkable authority the participant can reach, an office with a street address (500 Indiana Avenue NW, Room 4001) and a telephone number, with the Seal Team at criminalmotionsealteam@dcsc.gov named alongside it. It is not the "check with the court" gesture the standard excludes, because it names who answers. My earlier FAIL demanded a figure the repository does not hold, which is the invention every other rule here forbids; dc_seal_fugitive-set passed on this identical sentence, and a family's terminal state cannot turn on which verifier read it.

SERVICE.finding: Re-examined under the determination's extension to SERVICE and reversed. A named checkable authority stands in for a rule no held source establishes, for both halves of the obligation. FILING_DESTINATION.finding: Kept on re-examination, and the ground is stated exactly. The instructions never name where the motion is filed: step 4 says "File the motion with the tendered order", which states what accompanies what, and no line says the filing goes to the circuit court clerk or to the county of conviction. The fact is held elsewhere in this repository - the committed legal-design track registry entry for ky_void_seal_controlled_substance states the destination in terms ("Office of the Circuit Court Clerk... filed in the original criminal case in the county of conviction", with the Clerks' Manual filing type recorded) - so this is a fact the build holds and does not carry onto the participant-facing page, and the repair is to state it. Boundary noted rather than decided: DET-FEE-AND-WAIVER-001 extends its named-authority reasoning to FEE_AND_WAIVER and SERVICE only, and this packet does name the circuit court clerk for the county in the caption as an authority to ask - about service and about the fee, not about where to file. If Captain extends that reasoning to FILING_DESTINATION, this finding should be revisited; on the determination as written it stands.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.finding: Re-examined against DET-FEE-AND-WAIVER-001 and reversed. The packet states that it does not hold the figure and names who does: "The filing fee, and any deadline. Ask the same clerk. No amount and no number of days is stated here, because an unsourced figure in a filing instruction is worse than none." "The same clerk" is the authority named in the bullet immediately above it - the circuit court clerk for the county in the caption - and the caption is one the packet itself fills, so the office resolves to a determinate, reachable clerk rather than a gesture. The stated reason for withholding a figure is the same principle the determination endorses. This obligation no longer contributes to this family's failure.

SERVICE.finding: Re-examined under the determination's extension to SERVICE and reversed. Both halves are delegated to one named, reachable authority rather than left blank. Recipient: "Ask the circuit court clerk for the county in the caption who must receive a copy", repeated on the certificate of service page itself. Method: the instructions state the ordinary options and the authority that settles them - "by hand, by first-class mail, or whatever method the clerk tells you this filing requires". The packet is explicit that the order form it is built from does not establish the service rule, which is why it names the clerk instead of inventing a recipient. This obligation no longer contributes to this family's failure.
